newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Orbital says amortisation hits profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Orbital says amortisation hits profit.

text.p: Engine designer Orbital Engine Corp Ltd said on Friday that its decision to amortise intangibles from January 1996 to June 1999 will result in significantly lower earnings in the short term.
The company recorded abnormal expenses of A$69.04 million for the half year to December 31, contributing to a loss of A$93.92 million for the period.

The expense related to the amortisation of cash expenditures on patents, licences, and technologies of A$16.59 million and patents licences and technologies arising from restructurings of A$52.45 million.

"As shareholders will be aware, over the last two years Orbital has sought to eliminate the large intangible asset values from its balance sheet (A$382.86 million as of June 30, 1995)," the company said.
"Shareholders approved measures to effect this at the 1995 annual general meeting, however subsequent developments have resulted in that course being only partially implemented," Orbital said.

"Directors have since resolved to eliminate all intangibles, whether arising from cash or non-cash transactions by amortising these amounts over the period 1 January 1996 to 30 June 1999," the company said.
"This results in large amortisation charges which overwhelm the cash flows, revenues and costs for the period," it said.

"In the short term, these amortisation charges mean that Orbital will report significantly lower earnings in Australia," it said. "However, in the longer term Orbital will report reduced amortisation charges and declare dividends earlier than if these policies were not adopted," it said.
Orbital reported a net loss of A$17.77 million in the half year to December 31, 1995.
For the latest full year to June 30, 1996 the net loss came in at A$69.83 million.
The company reported sales of A$15.39 million for the latest half year, up from A$13.48 million a year earlier.
